blocks.text: The Application Investigation Inventory tracks application usage and provides detailed Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) data through an intuitive drill-down interface, facilitating essential security auditing, compliance, and threat identification.
The Inventory page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Gain insights into executable files and applications stored on endpoints.
Gather data on installed software, running processes, and libraries.

blocks.text: On the Inventory page (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint Data Scan > Application Investigation > Inventory), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Filter the data for a specific Product Name, OS, Code Signing Certificate Status, Threat Type, Category, Vulnerabilities, or Application Name. You can add filters by clicking the Add icon (). The available option is Application Name.
Gain visibility into:
Detected Applications: The number of applications detected on Windows and macOS.
Applications by Threat Type: The application distribution, categorized by threat types.
Applications by Code Signing Status: The application distribution, categorized by the code signing certificate status.
Export the data to a CSV file.
View a list of applications for an endpoint. For each application, you can filter by:

Application Name: The name of the application or executable file. Click the name to open a drawer that shows details of that application or executable file. To learn more, see Analyzing Application Details.
Product Name: The product name associated with the application or executable file.
Last Execution: The timestamp of the application's most recent execution.
Code Signing Certificate Status: The code signing status of the application (i.e., Valid Signature, Certificate Expired, Unsigned, Not Valid, or Invalid Signature).
Category: The functional classification used to group the application.
Distinct Versions: The software version currently running on the application.
Instances: The number of detected application instances.

Vulnerabilities: The level of the vulnerabilities listed by severity (i.e., Low, Medium, High, or Critical) based on the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) rating. To learn more, refer to About CVE Program.
Threat Type: The threat type of the application (i.e., Benign, Malicious, Suspicious, or Unknown).

The endpoint detects the application threat type by performing a local signature check to instantly verify applications from trusted providers. If a signature is unknown or compromised, ZDP automatically consults the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange, which cross-references the file against global threat feeds, proprietary intelligence, and an extensive sandbox history to determine a final safety verdict (Benign, Suspicious, Malicious, or Unknown).
Select, deselect, or order the data fields displayed in the table.
Modify the table and its columns.
Go to the Application Investigation Overview page.

blocks.text: Use the arrows at the bottom of the page to go to view the next entries. You can also select the number of entries you want to view in the table (15, 25, 50, or 100 rows).
